title: Motion for Leave to Reply and Reply of  American Transmission Company LLC to the Answers filed by Microsoft Corporation et al. re the 07/24/2026 tariff filing under ER26-3265.

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


American Transmission Company LLC                                     Docket No. ER26-3265-000


                       MOTION FOR LEAVE TO REPLY AND REPLY OF
                        AMERICAN TRANSMISSION COMPANY LLC

          Pursuant to Sections 212 and 213 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 1

American Transmission Company LLC (ATC) by its corporate manager, ATC Management Inc.

(collectively, ATC) hereby files this Motion for Leave to Reply and Reply to the Answers filed

by Microsoft Corporation (Microsoft), Data Center Coalition (DCC). 2 On July 24, 2026, ATC

filed four executed Amended Large Load Project Commitment Agreements (Amended LLPCAs)

and an executed Minimum Transmission Charge Agreement (MTCA) between ATC and

Wisconsin Electric Power Company (WEPCo) related to WEPCo’s service to Microsoft. As

discussed below, ATC’s filing is just and reasonable and should be accepted by the Commission

without a hearing or settlement proceedings with an effective date of July 1, 2026.

I.        REPLY

          ATC has worked collaboratively with WEPCo and Microsoft to develop a project

description and accelerated schedule that is responsive to Microsoft’s needs. 3 Since ATC’s initial

filing, ATC has addressed Microsoft’s concerns by agreeing to revise the Early Termination Fee


1
    18 C.F.R. § 385.212-213 (2026).
2
 Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer of Microsoft Corporation (Microsoft Answer) filed on Sept.
14, 2026), Motion of for Leave to Answer and Answer of the Data Center Coalition (DCC Answer) (filed
on Sept. 18, 2026, but incorrectly dated Aug. 18, 2026).
3
 Protest and Motion for Hearing and Settlement Judge Procedures of Microsoft Corporation, (Microsoft
Protest) at 1 (“Microsoft appreciates the ongoing collaboration of ATC and Wisconsin Electric Power
Company, dba We Energies (“WEPCo”), as they continue working with Microsoft to effectuate service
necessary to power Microsoft’s datacenter campus in Racine County, Wisconsin.”).
 and clarify the Security requirements. Hearing and settlement proceedings would serve no

apparent purpose other than potentially preventing proper cost allocation that protects other

ratepayers from paying for upgrades to ATC’s system caused by Microsoft’s load.

       Despite the parties’ disagreements, the Commission has a sufficient record to decide this

matter. ATC’s disagreement with certain characterizations advanced by Microsoft and other

intervenors does not create a genuine issue of material fact requiring a hearing. Indeed, the table

on pages 3–4 of Microsoft’s protest confirms that its purported factual disputes are legal or

policy questions that can be resolved on the pleadings. For example, no hearing or settlement

procedures are needed to determine that the LLPCAs and the MTCA are bilateral service

agreements binding only WEPCo, rather than generally applicable rate schedules. Under

Microsoft’s reasoning, every generator interconnection pre-agreement—including FCAs, FSAs,

and EPC agreements—would constitute a rate schedule. Moreover, most of the alleged factual

disputes merely concern the operation of the MISO Tariff. 4 Although protests routinely identify

disagreements in Section 205 proceedings, it is well established that “mere conjecture does not

create a genuine issue of material fact warranting a hearing.” 5 Any factual dispute presented

here—although none appears to exist—can be resolved on the written record. ATC’s proposed




4
  E.g., ATC’s statement that “Like any other Network Customer, ATC will charge WEPCO for Network
Service based on its load ratio share for as long as WEPCo uses that service, regardless of the
depreciation level of any particular transmission facilities.”
5
 Interstate Power & Light Co., 127 FERC 61,043 at P 44, n. 49 (2009) (finding that a protestor has a
burden to do more than make mere unsubstantiated allegations to warrant a hearing); Tenneco Oil Co. 25
FERC ¶ 61,234 (1983); Tilden Mining Co.L.C., v. Midcontinent Indep. System Op., Inc., 153 FERC
61,248 at P 22 (2015).

                                                  2
 approach follows the Transmission Security Agreement framework the Commission has already

accepted in other proceedings without a hearing. 6

          Finally, ATC is currently incurring costs to construct and operate the transmission

facilities needed to provide the capacity requested for Microsoft’s service. Non-large-load

customers are bearing costs that otherwise would be allocated to WEPCo, and hearing and

settlement proceedings would prolong that burden.

II.       MOTION FOR LEAVE TO REPLY

          ATC respectfully requests leave to submit this Reply. The Commission’s Rules of

Practice and Procedure prohibit answers to protests unless otherwise authorized. 7 The

Commission regularly allows answers for good cause shown, such as when the answers help

ensure a more accurate and complete record, clarify the issues, or provide useful and relevant

information that will assist the Commission in its deliberative process. 8 ATC’s Answer will

clarify the record, correct misinformation and ensure a more accurate and complete record.

Because this information will assist the Commission in its decision-making, ATC respectfully

requests that the Commission accept this Answer for good cause shown.




6
 See e.g., PECO Energy Co., 195 FERC 61,074 (2026); Commonwealth Edison Co., 194 FERC 1,183
(2026); see also Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator. Inc., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,212 at P 83 (2026) (Order
Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act) (Show Cause Order).
7
    18 C.F.R. § 385.213(a)(2).
8
  See, e.g., Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., 191 FERC ¶ 61,131 at P 24 (2025) (accepting answers
to answers “because they have provided information that assisted us in our decision-making process”);
Texas Eastern Transmission, LP, 122 FERC ¶ 61,205 at P 8 (2008) (accepting answer that completed the
record); California Indep. Operator Corp., 105 FERC ¶ 61,284 at P 10 (2003) (accepting MISO’s answer
that clarified the issues).

                                                    3
 IV.      CONCLUSION

         For the foregoing reasons, ATC respectfully requests that the Commission grant leave to

Reply, accept this Reply, deny the requests for hearing and settlement judge procedures, and

accept the Amended LLPCAs and the MTCA as just and reasonable, effective July 1, 2026.

                                     Respectfully submitted,
